meta.title: Pedestrians, passengers and pedestrian crossings
meta.summary: You will learn how the Rules require pedestrians and passengers to behave and, most importantly, what a driver must do at pedestrian crossings and at stops for route vehicles.

p: Pedestrians walk on pavements or footpaths, and if there are none, on the shoulders ⟦19⟧.
list: If there is no pavement, footpath or shoulder, or if it is impossible to walk on them, pedestrians walk on the cycle track or in single file along the edge of the carriageway. On a road with a central reservation, they walk along the outer edge.
People carrying bulky objects and people in non-motorised wheelchairs may move along the edge of the carriageway if they would obstruct other pedestrians on the pavement or shoulder.
Outside built-up areas, a pedestrian walking on the carriageway moves facing oncoming traffic. This way they can see the vehicles approaching them.
A person using a non-motorised wheelchair, or pushing a motorcycle, moped or bicycle along the edge of the carriageway, moves along the right-hand side of the road in the direction of traffic.
lesson.tip: Outside built-up areas, a pedestrian walks towards you, but a person pushing a bicycle or moped walks in the direction of traffic, with their back to you. Such a person is especially easy to miss.

p: Such a group walks on the carriageway in the direction of traffic, on the right-hand side, no more than 4 people abreast ⟦20⟧. At the front and rear of the group, on its left-hand side, there are escorts with red flags and, during the hours of darkness and in poor visibility, with lights switched on: white at the front and red at the rear.
Drivers are prohibited from crossing organised convoys and organised groups of pedestrians, and from joining them ⟦21⟧.

list: Pedestrians cross the carriageway at pedestrian crossings, including underground crossings and footbridges. If there is no crossing within sight, they cross at an intersection along the line of the pavements or shoulders ⟦22⟧.
If there is neither a crossing nor an intersection within sight, they may cross at right angles to the edge of the carriageway where the road can be clearly seen in both directions ⟦23⟧.
Crossing away from a pedestrian crossing is not allowed where there is a central reservation in a built-up area, or where pedestrian or road barriers are installed ⟦24⟧.
Where traffic is controlled, pedestrians follow the signals of the traffic controller or the pedestrian traffic light, and if there is none, the vehicle traffic light ⟦25⟧.

At an uncontrolled crossing, a pedestrian steps onto the road only after judging the distance to approaching vehicles and their speed and making sure that it is safe to cross. Away from a crossing, a pedestrian must not impede traffic or step out from behind a stationary vehicle or another obstruction that blocks the view ⟦26⟧.

A pedestrian must not linger on the carriageway without a reason related to safety. If they do not manage to finish crossing, they stop on the line separating traffic flows in opposite directions and continue only after making sure it is safe, taking into account the signals of the traffic light or traffic controller ⟦27⟧.
lesson.tip: A pedestrian who has stopped on the line between opposing traffic flows may continue crossing as soon as they are sure it is safe. Drivers should be ready for this.

p: If a vehicle with a flashing blue and (or) red beacon and a siren switched on is approaching, pedestrians must not start crossing, and those already on the carriageway must give way to it and clear the carriageway (para. 19, as amended on 27.04.2026).

list: People wait for route vehicles and taxis on a raised boarding platform, or, if there is none, on the pavement or shoulder ⟦28⟧.
Where there is no raised platform, people may step onto the carriageway to board only after the vehicle has stopped. After alighting, they must clear the carriageway immediately ⟦29⟧.

Passengers get in and out on the pavement or shoulder side, and only after the vehicle has come to a full stop. On a one-way street this may also be the left side, because in a built-up area stopping at the left-hand edge is permitted there ⟦30⟧. If it is impossible to get out on the pavement side, passengers may get out on the carriageway side, but only if it is safe and does not impede others ⟦31⟧.
A passenger in a vehicle fitted with seat belts wears a seat belt, and a passenger on a motorcycle or moped wears a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦32⟧.

Passengers are prohibited from distracting the driver while the vehicle is moving, from opening the doors and leaning out of windows and roof hatches while moving, from standing or sitting on the sides or on a load higher than the sides in the load body of a truck, and from standing on the footrests or the seat of a motorcycle or moped while it is moving ⟦33⟧.

lesson.h: The driver at an uncontrolled crossing
p: At a crossing without a traffic light or traffic controller, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway for the driver's direction of travel ⟦34⟧. To give way means not to force a pedestrian to change speed or direction ⟦35⟧. On a road with a central reservation, the carriageway for your direction is the one on your side of the reservation.

If a vehicle in the adjacent lane has stopped or slowed down before a crossing, you may continue only after making sure that there are no pedestrians in front of it ⟦36⟧. That vehicle may be hiding a person who is already walking across the crossing.

A crossing whose traffic light is flashing amber or not working counts as uncontrolled, just like an intersection ⟦37⟧. A person pushing a bicycle, moped, motorcycle or e-scooter, pulling or pushing a sledge, handcart or pram, or using a wheelchair also counts as a pedestrian ⟦38⟧.
lesson.tip: If the car in the next lane is braking before a zebra crossing, there is most likely a pedestrian there. Slow down and be ready to stop.

list: When your signal changes to one that allows you to go, pedestrians may still be finishing crossing the carriageway for your direction. You must give way to them ⟦39⟧.
You must not drive onto a pedestrian crossing if there is a traffic jam beyond it that would force you to stop right on the crossing ⟦40⟧.
lesson.tip: A green light does not mean “go at once”. First let pedestrians finish crossing and check that there is room beyond the zebra crossing.

p: When turning right or left, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway of the road they are turning into, and to cyclists on a cycle track crossing it ⟦41⟧. This applies both at controlled intersections and where there is no zebra crossing: if there is no crossing nearby, a pedestrian is entitled to cross at an intersection along the line of the pavements ⟦42⟧.
When your light turns green, first let through the vehicles that are finishing crossing the intersection and the pedestrians who have not finished crossing ⟦43⟧.
lesson.tip: When turning, watch not only for oncoming vehicles but also for the crossing on the road you are entering: pedestrians there often have their own green light.

list: The driver must give way to totally blind pedestrians signalling with a white cane in all cases, including away from pedestrian crossings ⟦44⟧.

When approaching a stationary vehicle displaying the “Carriage of children” sign, the driver must slow down, stop if necessary and let the group of children pass ⟦45⟧. The rule applies whichever side of the road the bus is on. Buses carrying organised groups of children are fitted with an amber beacon and “Carriage of children” signs at the front and rear ⟦46⟧.

p: If a bus, trolleybus or tram is standing at a stop and passengers are boarding and alighting directly from the carriageway or from a boarding platform located on it, the driver must give way to pedestrians walking to or from it on the door side ⟦47⟧.
lesson.tip: Take special care at stops without a raised platform: people walk to and from the vehicle directly on the carriageway.

keyFacts: Outside built-up areas, a pedestrian on the carriageway walks facing oncoming traffic, while a person pushing a bicycle, moped or motorcycle keeps to the right-hand side in the direction of traffic ⟦1⟧.
An organised group of pedestrians walks in the direction of traffic, on the right, no more than 4 abreast; drivers must not cross it or join it ⟦2⟧.
Crossing the road away from a crossing is not allowed where there is a central reservation in a built-up area, or where barriers are installed ⟦3⟧.
At an uncontrolled crossing, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway for the driver's direction of travel ⟦4⟧.
A crossing with a flashing amber or non-working traffic light counts as uncontrolled ⟦5⟧.
If a vehicle in the adjacent lane has stopped or slowed down before a crossing, you may drive on only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of it ⟦6⟧.
At a controlled crossing, when the signal allows you to go, you must give way to pedestrians who are finishing crossing ⟦7⟧.
When turning right or left, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the road they are turning into ⟦8⟧.
You must not drive onto a crossing if there is a traffic jam beyond it and you would have to stop on the crossing ⟦9⟧.
Always give way to a blind pedestrian with a white cane, even away from a crossing ⟦10⟧.
Approaching a stationary vehicle with the “Carriage of children” sign: slow down, stop if necessary and let the children pass ⟦11⟧.
Passengers get out on the pavement or shoulder side, and only after a full stop ⟦12⟧.
mistakes: Driving past a car that has stopped in the next lane before a zebra crossing, without slowing down. You may go on only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of it ⟦13⟧.
Moving off on green without giving way to pedestrians who are finishing crossing ⟦14⟧.
Driving onto a crossing when there is a traffic jam beyond it, hoping to “squeeze through”, and ending up stuck on the zebra crossing. This is prohibited ⟦15⟧.
Thinking that away from a crossing you never have to give way to a pedestrian. You must give way to a blind person with a white cane anywhere ⟦16⟧.

Letting a passenger out on the carriageway side without making sure it is safe. Passengers must get out on the pavement or shoulder side, and on the road side only if it is safe and does not impede anyone ⟦17⟧.
Turning on green while watching only oncoming vehicles. There may be pedestrians on the crossing of the road you are entering, and you must give way to them ⟦18⟧.

questions.q: You are approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing. A pedestrian has just stepped onto the carriageway for your direction. What must you do?
options: Drive through before they reach your lane
Sound the horn so that they stop
Give way to the pedestrian
Drive around behind them
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway for the driver's direction of travel.

questions.q: You are driving in the left lane. In the right lane, a truck has stopped before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing and is blocking your view. What should you do?
options: Keep your speed: your lane is clear
Proceed only after making sure no pedestrians are in front of the truck
Move in behind the truck and wait until it has driven over the crossing
Sound the horn and drive over the crossing without slowing down
questions.explain: If a vehicle has stopped or slowed down before an uncontrolled crossing, drivers in the adjacent lanes may continue only after making sure that there are no pedestrians in front of it.

questions.q: Before an uncontrolled crossing, a car in the adjacent lane has slowed down. You can clearly see that there is no one in front of it or on the crossing. May you continue?
options: Yes, since you have made sure no one is in front of it
No, you must stop without fail, like that car
No, you must wait until that car has gone through first
questions.explain: The rule requires not a compulsory stop but a check: you may continue once you have made sure that there are no pedestrians in front of the vehicle that has stopped or slowed down.

questions.q: At a controlled pedestrian crossing, your light has turned green. A pedestrian is still finishing crossing the carriageway for your direction. What should you do?
options: Move off: your light is green
Sound the horn so that the pedestrian hurries up
Drive around behind the pedestrian without waiting for them to finish
Let the pedestrian finish crossing
questions.explain: At a controlled crossing, when the signal permitting you to go comes on, the driver must give way to pedestrians finishing crossing the carriageway for the driver's direction.

questions.q: You are approaching a pedestrian crossing on a green light. Right beyond the crossing, vehicles are stationary: there is a traffic jam and no room for you beyond the crossing. What should you do?
options: Drive onto the crossing and wait there
Drive onto it if there are no pedestrians on the crossing
Do not drive onto the crossing; stop before it
Drive onto it with your hazard warning lights switched on
questions.explain: Driving onto a pedestrian crossing is prohibited if there is a traffic jam beyond it that would force you to stop on the crossing.

questions.q: Away from a pedestrian crossing, a person with a white cane starts crossing the road in front of you. What should you do?
options: Drive on: away from a crossing, pedestrians must give way to vehicles
Sound the horn to warn them
Drive around them without slowing down
Let the pedestrian cross, stopping if necessary
questions.explain: In all cases, including away from pedestrian crossings, the driver must give way to totally blind pedestrians signalling with a white cane.

questions.q: A tram is standing at a stop without a boarding platform, and passengers are getting off directly onto the carriageway. You are travelling in the same direction. What must you do?
options: Give way to pedestrians walking to and from the tram
Drive between the tram and the pavement, sounding the horn
Drive past slowly if no one is standing right in front of your car
Drive around the tram on the left in the oncoming lane
questions.explain: The driver must give way to pedestrians walking to or from a route vehicle standing at a stop on the door side, if boarding and alighting take place from the carriageway.

questions.q: You are approaching a stationary bus with the “Carriage of children” sign. There are children near it. What must you do?
options: Drive past at the same speed, keeping a lateral clearance
Slow down, stop if necessary and let the children pass
Sound the horn and drive past
Stop only if the bus has its hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: When approaching a stationary vehicle with the “Carriage of children” sign, the driver must slow down, stop if necessary and let the group of children pass.

questions.q: You are driving on a road outside a built-up area with no pavements or shoulders. A pedestrian is walking along the edge of the carriageway. How must they walk under the Rules?
options: Facing oncoming traffic
In the direction of traffic
On either side, whichever is more convenient
In the middle of the lane, so as to be more visible
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, when moving on the carriageway, pedestrians walk facing oncoming traffic.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area, a person is pushing a bicycle along the edge of the carriageway. On which side and in which direction must they walk?
options: On the left-hand side, facing oncoming traffic
On either side: they count as a pedestrian
On the right-hand side, in the direction of traffic
questions.explain: A person pushing a motorcycle, moped or bicycle along the edge of the carriageway keeps to the right-hand side of the road in the direction of traffic. The “facing oncoming traffic” rule does not apply to them.

questions.q: An organised group of pedestrians with escorts is walking on the right-hand side of the carriageway. You need to turn right, and the group is just passing the turning. What should you do?
options: Drive through the group if there is a gap in it
Wait for the group to pass: crossing it is prohibited
Sound the horn so that the group stops
Join the group and move along with it up to the turning
questions.explain: Drivers are prohibited from crossing organised convoys and organised groups of pedestrians, and from joining them.

questions.q: A city street has a central reservation. A pedestrian wants to cross the street far from a pedestrian crossing. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if they cross at right angles and the road is clearly visible
Yes, if there are no vehicles nearby and they impede no one
Yes, if they wait on the central reservation for traffic to pass
No: with a central reservation in town, only at a crossing
questions.explain: Crossing the carriageway away from a pedestrian crossing is not allowed where there is a central reservation in a built-up area, or where barriers are installed.

questions.q: You have stopped by the pavement on the right to let a passenger out. Which side must they get out on?
options: On the pavement side, and only after a full stop
On either side, as the car has already stopped
On the carriageway side, if that is closer for them
On the pavement side, even before a full stop if the speed is low
questions.explain: Passengers get in and out on the pavement or shoulder side, and only after the vehicle has come to a full stop.

questions.q: While the car is moving, the front-seat passenger wants to open the door slightly to free some clothing caught in it. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the speed is low and the door is opened only a little
No: opening doors while the vehicle is moving is prohibited
Yes, if the driver does not object and is driving slowly
Yes, if there are no other vehicles behind or to the right
questions.explain: Passengers are prohibited from opening the doors and from leaning out of windows and roof hatches while the vehicle is moving.

questions.q: A person is walking across an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing in front of you, pushing a bicycle beside them. What should you do?
options: Drive on: a cyclist must give way to vehicles
Give way: they count as a pedestrian
Drive on if they have not yet reached the middle of your lane
Sound the horn so that they stop
questions.explain: The person is walking across the zebra crossing in your lane. Someone pushing a bicycle is treated as a pedestrian, and the driver must give way to pedestrians at an uncontrolled crossing.

questions.q: The traffic light at a pedestrian crossing is flashing amber. A pedestrian has stepped off the pavement onto the crossing. What should you do?
options: Drive on: a flashing amber light permits movement without restrictions
Give way: such a crossing counts as uncontrolled
Drive on if the pedestrian has not yet reached the middle of your lane
Stop only if the pedestrian signals with their hand
questions.explain: A flashing amber signal means that the crossing is not controlled by the traffic light. So the rule for uncontrolled crossings applies: you must give way to a pedestrian who is crossing your carriageway.

questions.q: On a street with a central reservation, a pedestrian is walking across an uncontrolled crossing. Must you give way to them?
options: Yes: they are crossing the carriageway for your direction
No: they have not yet reached your lane
No: they are crossing the carriageway for oncoming traffic
Yes, but only if they signal with their hand
questions.explain: The pedestrian is already on the carriageway for your direction, to the right of the central reservation, and is walking towards your lane. You must give way to them, even if for now they are in the adjacent lane.

questions.q: On a street with a central reservation, a pedestrian is walking across an uncontrolled crossing. Must you give way to them?
options: Yes: they are crossing the carriageway for your direction
No: they have not yet reached your lane
No: they are crossing the carriageway for oncoming traffic
Yes, but only if they signal with their hand
questions.explain: The pedestrian is walking on the carriageway for oncoming traffic, beyond the central reservation, and is moving away from you. They are not crossing the carriageway for your direction, so you may continue without impeding them. It is the white car that must give way to them.

questions.q: To your left, a white car has stopped before an uncontrolled crossing. What must you do?
options: Carry on: your lane before the crossing is clear
Drive over the crossing after slowing to about 20 km/h
Sound the horn and drive on without changing lanes
Stop to let the pedestrian heading for your lane cross
questions.explain: The white car has stopped to let a pedestrian cross and is hiding them from you. You may drive on only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of it. Here the pedestrian is walking towards your lane, so you must stop.

questions.q: You are waiting before a controlled crossing, and your light has just turned green. A pedestrian in the adjacent lane has not yet finished crossing. What should you do?
options: Move off: the pedestrian is not in your lane
Sound the horn and move off on green
Let the pedestrian finish crossing
Move off slowly, driving around behind the pedestrian
questions.explain: A green signal does not cancel your duty to give way to pedestrians who are finishing crossing the carriageway for your direction. The pedestrian is walking towards your lane, so you must not move off yet.

questions.q: There is a traffic jam right beyond an uncontrolled crossing, and there are no pedestrians on the crossing. May you drive onto the crossing and wait there?
options: Yes: there are no pedestrians, and you are not impeding anyone
Yes, if you switch on your hazard warning lights
No: you must wait before the crossing
Yes, if you stay there for no more than a minute
questions.explain: There is no room beyond the crossing: the blue car is standing almost at the zebra crossing. The ban on driving onto a crossing when there is a traffic jam beyond it also applies when no pedestrians are in sight. A car standing on the crossing will block it for people who arrive later.

questions.q: Your light is green. A person with a white cane is slowly walking across the crossing in front of you, although their light is red. What should you do?
options: Drive on: your light is green and the pedestrian is breaking the rules
Sound the horn to warn them
Let the pedestrian cross, even though your light is green
Drive around them in the oncoming lane
questions.explain: The driver must give way to a totally blind pedestrian signalling with a white cane in all cases, even when the driver's own light is green. Such a person cannot see the traffic light.

questions.q: On the opposite side of the road, a bus with the “Carriage of children” sign has stopped. Children are crossing the road in front of it. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the rule only applies to those driving behind the bus
Drive on closer to the right-hand edge without slowing down
Sound the horn so that the children stop
Slow down, stop and let the children cross
questions.explain: The requirement to slow down, stop if necessary and let the group of children pass does not depend on which side of the road the bus is on. The children are already stepping into your lane. Such buses are fitted with an amber beacon ⟦48⟧.

questions.q: A bus is standing at a stop on your right, and passengers are getting off. You are driving past in the adjacent lane. What should you be ready for?
options: Nothing special: the passengers get off onto the pavement
The bus being obliged to give way to you when it pulls away
The bus suddenly starting to reverse
A pedestrian stepping out onto the road from behind the bus
questions.explain: Pedestrians are prohibited from stepping onto the road from behind a stationary vehicle without making sure it is safe, but in practice this often happens. When driving past a stationary bus, slow down and be ready to brake. And in a built-up area, it is you who must give way to a bus pulling away from a stop ⟦49⟧.

questions.q: You are turning right at an uncontrolled intersection. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the pedestrian
Only the white car
The pedestrian and the white car
No one
questions.explain: When turning right, you drive across the crossing on the road you are turning into, so you give way to the pedestrian walking across it. The white car is going straight on from the opposite direction and does not cross your path.

questions.q: You are going straight on through an uncontrolled intersection. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the pedestrian
Only the white car
The pedestrian and the white car
No one
questions.explain: You are not turning and do not drive across the crossing on the road to the right, so you do not impede the pedestrian there. The white car is going straight on towards you, and your paths do not cross.

questions.q: You are turning left at an intersection of roads of equal status. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the pedestrian
Only the white car
The pedestrian and the white car
No one
questions.explain: The oncoming white car is going straight on, and when turning left you must give way to oncoming vehicles going straight on or turning right. You must also give way to the pedestrian crossing the road you are turning into.

questions.q: There is no pedestrian crossing at the intersection. You are turning right, and a pedestrian is crossing the road you are turning into along the line of the pavements. Who must you give way to?
options: No one: the pedestrian is not on a pedestrian crossing
Only the pedestrian
Only the green car
The pedestrian and the green car
questions.explain: If there is no crossing nearby, a pedestrian is entitled to cross at an intersection along the line of the pavements. When turning, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway of the road they are turning into, even without a zebra crossing. The green car is turning right onto another road and is not in your way.

questions.q: Your light is green and you are going straight on. A person with a white cane is walking across the crossing on the road you are entering. Who must you give way to?
options: No one: you have a green light
Only the pedestrian with the white cane
Only the white car
Both the pedestrian and the white car
questions.explain: You must give way to a blind pedestrian with a white cane in all cases, even if their light is red. The white car is turning left from the opposite direction and must itself give way to you, since you are going straight on.

questions.q: The blue car in the right lane has stopped before a pedestrian crossing. You are in the left lane, going straight on. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the blue car
Only the pedestrian
No one: your lane is clear
The blue car and the pedestrian
questions.explain: The blue car has stopped to let a pedestrian cross and is hiding them from you. You may continue only after making sure there is no one in front of it. The pedestrian is walking towards your lane, so you must let them cross. The blue car is stationary, and you are not impeding it.

questions.q: You are coming out of a minor road and turning right. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the green car
Only the pedestrian
The green car and the pedestrian
No one
questions.explain: The green car is travelling on the main road in the direction you are turning, and under sign 2.4 you must give way to it. You must also give way to the pedestrian crossing the road you are turning into.

questions.q: Your light is green and you are turning right. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the white car
The white car and the pedestrian
Only the pedestrian
No one
questions.explain: The pedestrian is walking across the crossing on the road you are turning into, and you must give way to them. The white car is turning left from the opposite direction, so it is the one that must give way to you.

questions.q: The traffic controller is standing with their right side towards you. You are turning right. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the pedestrian
Only the taxi
The pedestrian and the taxi
No one
questions.explain: The traffic controller is standing side-on to you and to the taxi: you are both allowed to go straight on and turn right, and pedestrians are allowed to cross the road. The taxi is going straight on and is not in your way, but you must give way to the pedestrian on the road you are turning into. The bus is stationary: the traffic controller has their back to it.

questions.q: The pavement is narrow and crowded, so a person in a non-motorised wheelchair is moving along the edge of the carriageway to your right. Are they breaking the Rules?
options: No: it is allowed if they would obstruct pedestrians on the pavement
Yes: pedestrians are never allowed to move on the carriageway
No, but only if the wheelchair has a light or a flag
Yes: along the edge of the carriageway they must face oncoming traffic
questions.explain: People in non-motorised wheelchairs and people carrying bulky objects may move along the edge of the carriageway if they would obstruct others on the pavement. On the edge of the road, they keep to the right-hand side in the direction of traffic, as here. Leave plenty of room when driving around such a person.

questions.q: An organised group of pedestrians with escorts is walking along the right-hand edge of a road outside a built-up area, in the same direction as you. The oncoming lane is clear. May you drive around the group?
options: No: you may only follow the group until it leaves the road
Yes, on the left, with a safe lateral clearance
No: you must stop and wait until the group has passed
Yes, but only after sounding a long blast of the horn
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit crossing an organised group and joining it, but they do not prohibit driving around it. Drive around slowly and with a wide clearance: people may suddenly step to the side.

questions.q: During the hours of darkness, an organised group of pedestrians is walking along the road. What lights must the escorts have?
options: Red at the front and rear
Red at the front, white at the rear
No lights are needed if the escorts have red flags
White at the front, red at the rear
questions.explain: Escorts with red flags walk at the front and rear of the group on its left-hand side. During the hours of darkness and in poor visibility, they have lights switched on: white for the front escort and red for the rear one, like the lights on a car.

questions.q: How does an organised group of pedestrians move on the carriageway?
options: On the left, facing oncoming traffic, no more than two abreast
In the middle of the carriageway, in any direction
On the right, facing oncoming traffic, no more than six abreast
On the right, with the traffic, no more than four abreast
questions.explain: An organised group of pedestrians moves in the direction of traffic on the right-hand side, no more than four abreast. In this it differs from a single pedestrian outside a built-up area, who walks facing oncoming traffic.

questions.q: A pedestrian is walking across a crossing, and an ambulance with its flashing beacons and siren on is approaching the crossing. What must the pedestrian do under the Rules?
options: Carry on crossing: on a zebra crossing they have priority
Stop in the middle of the lane so that the driver notices them
Run across in front of the ambulance as fast as possible
Give way to the ambulance and clear the carriageway
questions.explain: When a vehicle with a flashing blue and (or) red beacon and a siren switched on is approaching, pedestrians must not start crossing, and those already on the carriageway must give way to it and clear the carriageway. This also applies at a pedestrian crossing.

questions.q: Which signals on an approaching vehicle mean that a pedestrian must not start crossing, even at a pedestrian crossing?
options: Only a blue beacon, even if the siren is off
Any beacon, including an amber or yellow one
Hazard warning lights and main-beam headlights switched on
A blue and (or) red beacon together with a siren
questions.explain: Pedestrians must not cross the carriageway when a vehicle is approaching with a flashing blue and (or) red beacon switched on together with a special audible signal, that is, a siren (para. 19 as amended on 27.04.2026). An amber beacon and hazard warning lights have no such meaning.

questions.q: Where do passengers wait for a bus if there is no raised boarding platform at the stop?
options: On the pavement or shoulder
On the carriageway at the edge of the road
On the central reservation
Wherever convenient, as long as no bus is in sight
questions.explain: People wait for route vehicles and taxis on a raised boarding platform, or, if there is none, on the pavement or shoulder. You must not stand on the carriageway while waiting for a bus.

questions.q: A stop outside a built-up area has no boarding platform. People are waiting on the shoulder as the bus approaches. When may they step onto the carriageway to board it?
options: When the bus starts braking
As soon as the bus comes into view
They must not step onto the carriageway here at all
Only after the bus has stopped
questions.explain: At stops without a raised boarding platform, people may step onto the carriageway to board only after the vehicle has stopped. While the bus is moving, people stay on the shoulder.

questions.q: At a stop without a boarding platform, a passenger has got off the bus directly onto the carriageway. What must they do?
options: Wait on the carriageway until the bus has left
Stand by the door until all the passengers have got off
Leave the carriageway immediately, without delay
Cross the road right in front of the bus while it is stationary
questions.explain: After alighting, pedestrians must clear the carriageway without delay. They cross the road to and from the stop under the general rules for pedestrians and do not step out from behind a stationary bus without making sure that no vehicles are coming.

questions.q: On a one-way street, you have stopped by the left-hand pavement to let a passenger out. Which side should they get out on?
options: On the right: passengers must always get out on the right
On the left, on the pavement side
On either side, as the car is stationary
On the right, if there are no vehicles there
questions.explain: Passengers get in and out on the pavement or shoulder side. On a one-way road in a built-up area you may stop at the left-hand edge, and then the pavement is on the left: that is the side to get out on.

questions.q: You have stopped at the right-hand edge, but there is a barrier right next to the car on the right and the door cannot be opened. How should the passenger get out?
options: On the carriageway side, if it is safe and does not impede anyone
They cannot: such alighting is prohibited, so find another place
On the carriageway side at once without looking back: vehicles must go around
Open the door and get out while the car is still rolling slowly
questions.explain: Passengers get out on the pavement or shoulder side, and only after a full stop. If it is impossible to get out on that side, they may get out on the carriageway side, but only when it is safe and will not impede other road users.

questions.q: A passenger in the back seat says there is no need to wear a seat belt in the back. Are they right?
options: Yes: seat belts are compulsory only in the front seats
Yes, if the journey is short and the speed is low
No: everyone must wear a seat belt if belts are fitted
Yes, if the driver has allowed them not to wear one
questions.explain: A passenger must wear a seat belt if the vehicle is fitted with seat belts, and the driver must not carry passengers who are not wearing seat belts. Where the passenger sits in the car does not matter.

questions.q: You are giving a friend a lift on a moped. They have a motorcycle helmet but do not want to fasten it, as it is not far. May you ride like this?
options: No: the passenger's helmet must be fastened
Yes, if the speed is no more than 30 km/h and the trip is short
Yes: the helmet must be fastened only outside built-up areas
Yes, if the helmet is on their head, even if unfastened
questions.explain: A passenger on a motorcycle or moped must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet, and the driver must not carry passengers without a fastened helmet. An unfastened helmet comes off in a fall and gives no protection.

questions.q: While the car is moving, a passenger shows the driver a video on their phone and asks them to watch it. What do the Rules say about this?
options: It is acceptable on a straight stretch of road with no bends
It is allowed if the driver keeps both hands on the wheel
The Rules govern only the driver's actions, not the passengers'
Passengers must not distract the driver while in motion
questions.explain: Passengers are prohibited from distracting the driver from driving while the vehicle is moving. Even one second of looking away at 60 km/h means more than 15 m driven blind.

questions.q: Workers are being carried in the load body of a dropside truck. One of them has sat on the side to be more comfortable. May they travel like this?
options: Yes, if they hold on tightly to the cab with one hand
Yes, if the truck is travelling no faster than 40 km/h
Yes, if the tailgate is securely locked shut
No: sitting on the sides while moving is prohibited
questions.explain: Passengers of a dropside truck are prohibited from standing, sitting on the sides or on a load that is higher than the sides. When braking or on an uneven surface, a person can easily fall out of the load body.

questions.q: While the car is moving, a child in the back seat wants to lean out of the open sunroof. May you allow this?
options: Yes, if you are driving in a residential zone or a yard
Yes, if the speed is below 20 km/h and the road is straight
No: leaning out of a sunroof while moving is prohibited
Yes, if an adult is sitting next to the child and holding them
questions.explain: Passengers are prohibited from leaning out of the window openings and roof hatches of a vehicle while it is moving. A branch, a post or sudden braking can result in a serious injury.

questions.q: A motorcycle passenger has stood up on the footrests while moving to get a better view of the road. Is this allowed?
options: Allowed on a straight road when the speed is low
Allowed if the passenger holds on tightly to the driver
Prohibited: no standing on the footrests while moving
Allowed, but only outside built-up areas
questions.explain: Passengers on a motorcycle or moped are prohibited from standing on the footrests or on the seat while it is moving. This makes the motorcycle sway and makes it harder for the driver to control it.

questions.q: A pedestrian is carrying a large sheet of plywood and would obstruct others on the pavement. Where may they walk if the road has a central reservation?
options: On the central reservation
Along the outer edge of the carriageway
Along the edge of the carriageway next to the central reservation
In the middle of the carriageway
questions.explain: People carrying bulky objects and people in non-motorised wheelchairs may move along the edge of the carriageway if they would obstruct others on the pavement or shoulder. On a road with a central reservation, this is allowed only along the outer edge of the carriageway.

questions.q: The road has no pavement, footpath or shoulder, but there is a cycle track next to it. Where should a pedestrian walk?
options: On the cycle track or in single file along the edge of the carriageway
Only along the edge of the carriageway: not on the cycle track
Along the edge of the carriageway two or three abreast, with the traffic
In the middle of the carriageway if there is little traffic
questions.explain: If there are no pavements, footpaths or shoulders, or if it is impossible to walk on them, pedestrians walk on the cycle track or in single file along the edge of the carriageway.

questions.q: A road outside a built-up area has no pavement but has a shoulder. Where must a pedestrian walk?
options: On the shoulder, not on the carriageway
Along the edge of the carriageway in the direction of traffic
In the middle of the carriageway, so as to be more visible
On any part of the road if there is little traffic
questions.explain: Pedestrians walk on pavements or footpaths, and if there are none, on the shoulders. They go onto the carriageway only when there is nowhere else to walk, and then, outside built-up areas, they walk facing oncoming traffic.

questions.q: Where should a pedestrian cross the carriageway, first and foremost?
options: At pedestrian crossings, including underground ones
Anywhere the road is currently clear of vehicles
Only at intersections, along the line of the pavements
Wherever is nearest to the building or stop they need
questions.explain: Pedestrians cross the carriageway at pedestrian crossings, including underground crossings and footbridges. If there is no crossing within sight, they cross at an intersection along the line of the pavements or shoulders.

questions.q: There is neither a pedestrian crossing nor an intersection within sight. How should a pedestrian cross the road correctly?
options: Diagonally, so as to reach the other side more quickly
At right angles, where the road is visible in both directions
Just past a bend in the road, where vehicles slow down
From behind a stationary car, where the way across is shorter
questions.explain: If there is no crossing or intersection within sight, the road may be crossed at right angles to its edge on a stretch that can be clearly seen in both directions. That way the path across the carriageway is the shortest, and vehicles can be seen in advance.

questions.q: There is a pedestrian barrier in the middle of a city street, and the nearest crossing is far away. May a pedestrian climb over the barrier and cross here?
options: Yes, if no vehicles can be seen nearby at the moment
Yes, if they cross strictly at right angles
No: where there are barriers, only at a crossing
Yes by day, but not during the hours of darkness
questions.explain: Crossing the carriageway away from a pedestrian crossing is not allowed where pedestrian or road barriers are installed, and in a built-up area also where there is a central reservation.

questions.q: There are no pedestrian traffic lights at the intersection, only traffic lights for vehicles. Which signals does a pedestrian follow when crossing the road?
options: The signals of the vehicle traffic lights
None: without a pedestrian traffic light, crossing here is not allowed
They cross when there are no vehicles: traffic lights do not apply to them
Only a flashing amber signal
questions.explain: Where traffic is controlled, pedestrians follow the signals of the traffic controller or the pedestrian traffic light, and if there are none, the vehicle traffic light. In the diagram, the light is green for vehicles moving parallel to the pedestrian, and the crossing traffic is stopped.

questions.q: At an intersection, the pedestrian traffic light is working, but a traffic controller is directing traffic. Whose signals does a pedestrian obey?
options: The pedestrian traffic light's: it is intended specifically for pedestrians
Whichever signals allow crossing
The vehicle traffic light's
The traffic controller's: they override the traffic light
questions.explain: Drivers and pedestrians must obey the signals and instructions of the traffic controller, even if they contradict traffic light signals, road signs or road markings.

questions.q: How should a pedestrian step onto an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing?
options: At once: on a zebra crossing a pedestrian always has priority over vehicles
Only with a raised hand, so that drivers notice them in advance
After judging vehicles' distance and speed and making sure it is safe
Only when the nearest vehicle is more than a hundred metres away
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled crossing a pedestrian has priority, but they must step onto the road only after judging the distance to approaching vehicles and their speed. A driver who can no longer stop in time will be physically unable to give way.

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing the road away from a pedestrian crossing. What are they prohibited from doing?
options: Stepping out from behind a stationary car without checking
Walking at right angles to the edge of the carriageway
Crossing where the road can be seen in both directions
Crossing during the day when there is little traffic
questions.explain: Away from a pedestrian crossing, a pedestrian must not impede traffic or step out from behind a stationary vehicle or another obstruction that restricts the view without making sure that no vehicles are coming. The driver cannot see them because of the obstruction either.

questions.q: A pedestrian did not manage to finish crossing before the signal changed and has stopped on the centre line. What should they do next?
options: Run on before the vehicles move off
Go back to the pavement without looking at the vehicles
Stand in the middle of a traffic lane so that drivers go around them
Wait on the centre line and continue when it becomes safe
questions.explain: Pedestrians who have not managed to finish crossing stop on the line separating traffic flows in opposite directions and continue only after making sure it is safe, taking the traffic light signals into account. Drivers should remember that such a person is standing very close to their vehicle.

questions.q: When does a pedestrian crossing with a traffic light count as uncontrolled?
options: When the light flashes amber or is off, with no traffic controller
When the pedestrians' light is red and the vehicles' light is green
Only during the hours of darkness, when there is little traffic
When there are no pedestrians at all on or near the crossing
questions.explain: Controlled and uncontrolled crossings are distinguished in the same way as intersections: with a flashing amber signal, traffic lights that are not working or no traffic controller, a crossing is uncontrolled. Drivers then give way to pedestrians on it as at an ordinary zebra crossing.

questions.q: Which of the signs marks the actual location of a pedestrian crossing?
options: The left one, triangular
The right one, blue
Both signs
Neither: a crossing is marked only by road markings
questions.explain: The location of a crossing is marked by signs 5.16.1 and 5.16.2 and (or) zebra markings. The triangular sign 1.20 only warns of a crossing ahead. If there are no markings, the width of the crossing is the distance between signs 5.16.1 and 5.16.2.

questions.q: A tram is standing at a stop without a boarding platform, and its doors have already closed. A late passenger is running towards it across your lane. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the doors are closed, so boarding is over
Give way to the pedestrian running to the tram
Sound the horn so that they go back to the pavement
Drive around behind the pedestrian without slowing down
questions.explain: The driver must give way to pedestrians walking to or from a route vehicle standing at a stop if boarding takes place directly from the carriageway. The tram is still standing there, and the pedestrian is running to it across your lane, so you must let them pass.

questions.q: When must a driver give way to pedestrians walking to or from a tram standing at a stop?
options: If boarding is from the carriageway or a platform on it
Only if the tram sounded its horn before boarding
Only if the tram has its hazard warning lights on
Never: away from a crossing, pedestrians give way to vehicles
questions.explain: The driver must give way to pedestrians walking to or from a route vehicle standing at a stop on the door side, if boarding and alighting take place from the carriageway or from a boarding platform located on it. Route vehicles are buses, trolleybuses and trams.

questions.q: You are passing the “Children” sign near a school. What is the correct way to behave?
options: Drive as usual: the sign applies only during school hours
Sound the horn so that the children move away from the road
Slow down and be ready for children to appear
Move into the left lane and get through the section faster
questions.explain: Sign 1.21 “Children” warns of a section of road near a school, camp or other children's facility where children may appear on the carriageway. Children often run out suddenly and are poor at judging the speed of vehicles.

questions.q: Ahead of you, a pedestrian is running across the road away from a pedestrian crossing. They are breaking the Rules. What should you do?
options: Keep your speed: the pedestrian is the one breaking the rules
Sound the horn and carry on
Drive around them in the oncoming lane at the same speed
Slow down, even to the point of stopping
questions.explain: The pedestrian's violation does not release the driver from the duty to avoid hitting them. When there is a traffic hazard that the driver is able to detect, the driver must reduce speed, even to the point of stopping, or drive safely around the obstacle.

questions.q: Ahead of you, a bus with the “Carriage of children” sign and its amber beacon switched on is standing at the right-hand edge. No children can be seen near it yet. What must you do?
options: Nothing special: there are no children on the road
Slow down and be ready to stop
Stop and wait until the bus leaves
Sound the horn so that the bus driver notices you
questions.explain: When approaching a stationary vehicle with the “Carriage of children” sign, the driver must slow down and, if necessary, stop and let the group of children pass. Children may step out from behind the bus at any moment.

questions.q: You have stopped before an uncontrolled crossing to let a pedestrian cross. The driver behind you is impatiently sounding the horn. What should you do?
options: Drive on so as not to hold up the traffic
Let the pedestrian cross and only then drive on
Signal to the pedestrian to let the vehicles go first
Reverse a little to make room for the driver behind
questions.explain: The duty to give way to a pedestrian at an uncontrolled crossing does not depend on whether someone behind you is in a hurry. The horn of the driver behind does not give you the right to endanger the pedestrian.
